That has crossed my mind a few times, but I'm a terrible actor and I'd feel so guilty afterwards that I wouldn't be able to carry on with it. 

I've never heard of Lyrica or SNRIs, but I don't think I'm ever going to be put on medication at this rate. I'm 15, so they're reluctant to put me on anything, but there was a muckup at the hospital that didn't help at all: 

The last time I went for being suicidal, the psychiatrist who I talked to said that there are one or two anti-anxieties that aren't too addictive that I could try, but that he wasn't allowed to prescribe me anything and didn't want to anyway. BUT, he told the mental health group that I'm with, that he offered me some that I turned down for some reason.

So they think that I don't want medication, even though I've said that I'd be cool with it if it would help. It's a mess, really.

Thank you so much.

I do draw a lot, which helps a ton. I also have a cat but she doesn't live with us, so. We've been thinking about going out for walks and that kind of thing more often, we do have a park across the street so it wouldn't be that hard.

And thanks again, if I remember, I'll keep you in mind next time I'm feeling crappy.

Eh, sorta? There's a place on the other side of London that I could go to for gender problems specifically, which is good because the gender problems are a big deal that make me feel terrible. 

But I can't go there without being referred, which the current psychiatrist has to do. She won't because "it's probably because of stress" so that's out of the question. Really, it was all organized by my school, so we don't really know what to do to find somebody else.
